_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: a conversation's title renames it in place, in a bar as tall as a project's. Conversation {{ID}} has the slug {{SLUG}}. Call "slug" returns its slug from the server. Call "create-bar" creates project "{{NAME}}" through the API, and navigating to /test/go/bar then opens its settings (/project/<id>/settings). Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is {"role": "button", "name": "X", "exact": true}, with a "selector" to scope it when it is a row's, a menu's or a group's; but "there is no button X" counts {"role": "button", "name": "X"} without exact, so that a name containing X counts too. Texts that "are exactly [...]" are checked with assert_texts. "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. "The header" is the first ".header". "The title button T" is {"within": {"selector": ".header"}, "role": "button", "name": T, "exact": true}, and "the Rename field" {"within": {"selector": ".header"}, "role": "textbox", "name": "Rename", "exact": true}. 1. Navigate to /c/{{ID}}. 2. Click the title button {{SLUG}}. 3. The Rename field is focused (assert_focused), and its value is exactly "{{SLUG}}" (assert_value). 4. Fill the Rename field with "Discarded" and press Escape (press_key). 5. There is no Rename field (assert_count 0). 6. Click the title button {{SLUG}}, fill the Rename field with "titled 4f2a9c1e!" and press Enter. 7. The title button "titled-4f2a9c1e" is visible. 8. Call "slug" with expect "titled-4f2a9c1e". 9. Note the header's height, once: eval (no expect) of (() => { const h = document.querySelector(".header").getBoundingClientRect().height; sessionStorage.setItem("lcConversationBar", String(h)); return String(h); })(). 10. Call "create-bar" (no expect: it acts once), then navigate to /test/go/bar. 11. {"within": {"selector": "[data-testid='project-view']"}, "role": "button", "name": "{{NAME}}", "exact": true} is visible. 12. The view's header is exactly as tall, read once: eval (no expect) of (() => { const bar = Number(sessionStorage.getItem("lcConversationBar")); const headers = document.querySelectorAll("[data-testid='project-view'] .header"); if (headers.length !== 1) throw new Error("project view headers: " + headers.length); const h = headers[0].getBoundingClientRect().height; if (!bar || h !== bar) throw new Error("project bar " + h + ", conversation bar " + bar); return String(h); })().

steps.expression: (() => { const bar = Number(sessionStorage.getItem('lcConversationBar')); const headers = document.querySelectorAll("[data-testid='project-view'] .header"); if (headers.length !== 1) throw new Error('project view headers: ' + headers.length); const h = headers[0].getBoundingClientRect().height; if (!bar || h !== bar) throw new Error('project bar ' + h + ', conversation bar ' + bar); return String(h); })()
